scope: Frozen n134 source and modern text only, including all 17 prose objects, both languages, heading metadata, formulas, quantities, historical attribution and textual figure references.

integrityEvidence.method: Read-only byte hashes, parsed JSON equality, in-memory native edition checks and in-memory reconstruction from the frozen native page stream. Python used the existing lesson venv with -B; no validators that write artifacts were executed.

signatureChecks.independentSemanticCheckBeyondTokenSigna: All source and modern sentences checked for units, magnitudes, qualifications, direction, causality and historical attribution. The many-times wording issue is not detectable by numeric signatures.

findings.title: Make the historical Curie-value disclaimer explicit about reliability, not just precision
findings.reason: Attribution to the original textbook is present and is good. However, 'not as modern precision measurements' can still be read as endorsing these numbers as approximately reliable current values. The historical list is not a substitute for a present reference table; even the independently checked nickel reference does not reproduce the printed value. Make this distinction explicit instead of leaving the apparent disagreement to be explained only by precision or specimen composition.
findings.severityQualification: This is a recommended clarification of an existing disclaimer, not an allegation that the frozen prose presents the values without attribution.

replacementRecommended.operation: Replace the existing disclaimer sentence in each language, retaining the source list and the following composition/reference-data qualification.
replacementRecommended.zh: 这些数值仅作为原教材的历史记载保留，其中一些与目前通行的参考值并不一致；不能把它们作为当前材料的可靠居里温度，或仅仅视为精度较低的现代测量值。
replacementRecommended.en: These numbers are retained only as the original textbook's historical report. Some do not agree with reference values in current use; they must not be treated as reliable Curie temperatures for present-day materials, or merely as less precise modern measurements.

findings.title: The English heading is translated only in Markdown, not in title metadata
findings.reason: The English Markdown heading is an accurate translation, but the language=en template retains Chinese title metadata and has no separately represented English display title. Thus source identity passes while the requested complete English title-metadata coverage remains incomplete. This is not a reason to mutate protected identity fields: title and printed_title are explicitly immutable in the current native contract.

replacementRecommended.operation: Use the existing translated heading as the English display-title replacement only through an approved language-aware display-title binding. Until such a binding is authorized, keep metadata equivalence marked incomplete rather than claiming a full bilingual pass.

findings.title: Retain the many-times enhancement wording in English
findings.reason: The source and Chinese modern text describe a many-times increase. English 'can greatly strengthen' preserves the direction and practical significance but weakens that multiplicative comparison. No experimental multiplier should be invented.
findings.severityQualification: Minor translation precision issue, not a scientific contradiction.

replacementRecommended.operation: Replace only the English second sentence; leave the Chinese sentence and all existing comparison conditions unchanged.
replacementRecommended.en: At a temperature below the material's Curie temperature, inserting a suitable iron or steel core can strengthen the field inside a coil many times over while its current and winding geometry remain the same.

paragraphReviews.subject: Practical use and core-field enhancement
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Same current and winding geometry, suitable material below its Curie temperature, material contribution, and dependence on shape and magnetic state are explicit. No fixed universal enhancement factor is claimed.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: Equivalent conditions and causality; minor magnitude-wording replacement ZHEN-02.

paragraphReviews.subject: Relative permeability and remanence
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Permeability can be much greater than unity under suitable conditions, not at every field. Remanence is restricted to previously magnetized specimens; neither persistent coil current nor universally permanent unmagnetized material is asserted.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Can, some specimens, removed applied field and both cautions are preserved.

paragraphReviews.subject: Field-dependent and history-dependent effective permeability
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Fixed temperature and specimen shape do not make permeability a universal constant. Present field and prior magnetizing process are both required; this agrees with the later state-specific ratio and remanence explanation.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Neither language reduces the history dependence to just a single immediately preceding field value.

paragraphReviews.subject: Curie transition, historical temperatures and Curie identity
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: Spontaneous ferromagnetism disappearing above the transition is distinguished correctly from loss of every magnetic response. The heated-needle example concerns the conspicuous remanent attraction. All source values are retained and attributed, but the numerical disclaimer should be strengthened under SCI-01.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS for scientific meaning, numerical list, units and historical attribution. Both versions need the same recommended warning replacement.
paragraphReviews.historicalIdentity: The source-bound French scientist Curie is retained, with the literal source name in the English declaration. No unsupported discovery-priority or new personal details are added.

paragraphReviews.subject: Internal field, demagnetizing approximation and historical I units
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Long rod, sufficiently long solenoid, central approximately uniform aligned fields and negligible end-related demagnetizing effects are specified. B is total internal flux density; B0 is the same-current empty-coil field. Relative mu is a state-specific nonzero-field ratio, not differential permeability. I is a flux-density contribution, not current or SI magnetization measured in amperes per metre; conversion involves vacuum permeability.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. All geometry assumptions, the nonzero-field restriction, history restriction, definitions and unit cautions agree.

paragraphReviews.subject: Equation 13-2
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS within the preceding aligned-field and negligible-demagnetization model. The source expression I=B-B0 and its equation number are unchanged.

paragraphReviews.subject: Substitution of equation 13-1
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. The modern transition explicitly carries forward the model and specified nonzero applied-field state; it does not extrapolate the ratio to remanence at zero applied field.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Same substitution reference and restrictions.

paragraphReviews.subject: Equation 13-3
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. I=(mu-1)B0 follows algebraically from the two preceding relations at the specified nonzero-field state. The punctuation is outside math and the source formula and number are preserved.

paragraphReviews.subject: Experimentally determined magnetization curve
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. The curve is conditioned on temperature, shape and magnetizing procedure. Field and history dependence are explicit. The reference to section 133 is retained without promising a constant ratio for every experiment.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Definition, experimental method reference and procedure-dependence agree.

paragraphReviews.subject: Initial magnetization, saturation and domain explanation
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS as the source's qualitative initial-curve model. Demagnetized initial state, approximately zero net magnetization, fixed temperature below Curie, slow field change and approximate rather than exact saturation are stated. The initial approximately linear description is not an endorsement of linearity over the entire curve or every specimen. Saturation concerns the material contribution, not cessation of total-field growth. The loop-current picture is marked qualitative, mechanical electron-spin interpretation is rejected, and domain growth/reorientation is a sound qualitative explanation.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Both versions retain the initial approximation, saturation qualification, total-field distinction and domain-versus-mechanical-spin clarification.
paragraphReviews.figureQualification: Figure 301 is a textual reference only; no plotted slope, label or pixel was inspected.

paragraphReviews.subject: Material-specific curves and comparison conditions
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Material specificity is retained without implying that a material has one condition-independent immutable curve.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Temperature, shape, initial state and field procedure agree.

paragraphReviews.subject: Hysteresis, retained magnetization and obstructed domain motion
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Same present field may give different magnetic states. Descending from saturation need not retrace the initial curve; larger retained magnetization is qualified as usual, not universal. Pinning/impeded domain-wall motion and moment reorientation are valid qualitative causes. Removed applied field is not confused with zero internal field.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Same history variables, slow-field comparison and qualified domain explanation.

paragraphReviews.subject: Full hysteresis sequence, remanence, coercive field and symmetry
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS within the stated ideal model. Applied-field zero is distinguished from retained I and total internal B. A finite constant mu times zero is correctly rejected as a remanence argument. The reverse-field distance denotes magnitude. B0k is the source's flux-density-scaled reverse magnetizing field, not mechanical force or internal B; field-strength-unit conversion is acknowledged. The crossing is zero net magnetization while that reverse field is applied, not a demonstrated permanently demagnetized zero-field state. Symmetry is conditional on fixed temperature, no bias and equivalent forward/reverse procedures.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. All source mathematical labels, directions, sequence, remanence meaning, coercivity units and symmetry conditions are preserved.
paragraphReviews.figureQualification: oa, a, ab, ob, oc, a-prime and o are reviewed as source-bound text tokens only. Figure 302's actual labels, paths and symmetry remain unapproved.

paragraphReviews.subject: Stoletov attribution and closed-ring magnetization
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. A current-carrying winding magnetizes the iron ring; a closed magnetic path helps reduce open-rod end-related demagnetizing effects. Magnetization and conductor current are explicitly distinguished. The source's historical priority statement is attributed to the original textbook, not asserted as an independently established exclusive first.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. A. G. Stoletov, the retained source-name binding, Russian identity, source dates and experimental method are equivalent. Chinese 'earliest' and English 'first' are both explicitly the textbook's attribution.
paragraphReviews.historicalIdentity: The transliteration, initials and 1839-1896 source dates are preserved. No new dates, statistics or unsupported exclusive experimental priority are supplied.

paragraphReviews.subject: Different loop shapes
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Loop shape is useful for comparison but is explicitly conditioned on temperature, shape, history and field-changing conditions.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. The same caution against experiment-independent fixed shapes is present.

paragraphReviews.subject: Soft and hard magnetism, examples and permanent magnets
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS for textual science. Magnetic softness/hardness is separated from mechanical hardness. Iron, certain steels and permalloy are qualified examples, and permalloy is correctly identified as an iron-nickel alloy without inventing a composition percentage. Remanence differences are restricted to the source drawing; small loop area is explicitly not proof that every soft material has small remanence. Stable remanence and resistance to demagnetization explain permanent-magnet suitability under stated comparison conditions.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Figure-panel references are consistently localized to Latin a/b; material names, qualifications and the non-universal remanence caution agree.
paragraphReviews.figureQualification: Statements about the particular drawing remain conditional on the separate Figure 303 review. This review does not infer its pixels, scales, areas or intercepts.

paragraphReviews.subject: AC cores and correctly scaled hysteresis loss
paragraphReviews.scientificAssessment: PASS. Transformers, generators and motors are qualified uses; alternating-field operation is conditional. Loop area denotes per-volume, per-cycle hysteresis energy only with the correct axes and unit conversion, including vacuum permeability for the source's flux-density magnetization convention. Whole-core work also requires volume. A paper area is not joules. Soft/hard loss comparison is restricted to comparable amplitudes and conditions and is qualified as usual. Eddy-current and other losses prevent inferring total device loss solely from loop area.
paragraphReviews.bilingualAssessment: PASS. Units, volume, cycle, temperature/slow-field conditions and the total-loss caution are equivalent.

separateFigureGate.limits: Reference IDs, caption translations and diagram-related prose were checked as text. Hash-bound text and source integrity do not establish pixel fidelity, axis scales, labels, loop shape, dimensions, render quality or visual approval.

limitations: This is a text review, not source-pixel adjudication, visual acceptance or publication approval.
Source historical temperatures and exclusive historical priority remain source-attributed records. No new experimental table or exclusive-priority claim is endorsed.
The Curie-value recommendation is a reliability disclaimer, not a numerical erratum or authorization to change protected formula tokens.
English title coverage cannot be completed by directly changing title or printed_title under the current identity contract.
The source's qualitative initial-linearity model is not validated against unapproved Figure 301 pixels or treated as a universal linear constitutive law.

The HyperPhysics numerical-table fetch timed out and an initially guessed Cambridge introduction URL returned 404; neither was treated as evidence. Successful first-party text references are listed above.
New statistical examples, current replacement temperatures, composition percentages and unqualified universal material claims are absent from the recommendations.
